examples.title: Ordinary genus identification with unknown sex

specimen.evidence: Several good dorsal, lateral and frontal macro photographs

examples.situation: The user can answer broad Lucid characters but cannot determine sex and leaves difficult genital and fine-spine observations unknown.
expected: Record sex as Lucid state S004 without converting unanswered observations into absent scores.
Apply only characters that remain applicable under the Lucid dependencies.
Retain and rank all compatible Lucid genera rather than demanding an answer to every feature.
Explain which additional observable characters would best separate the leading candidates.
must_not: Invent a sex from photographs that do not establish it.
Treat unknown user answers as Lucid code 0.
Return a single genus merely because it is first in source order.

examples.title: Adult male enters the Saitis-group candidate region

specimen.evidence: Lucid observations leave Saitis-group genera among the leading candidates

examples.situation: Broad Lucid evidence narrows the specimen to the part of concept space covered by Schubert's male genus key and diagnostic assertions.
expected: Make the applicable Schubert male characters available automatically.
Continue the same identification session while preserving which observations came from which source ontology.
Use the Schubert key graph and reusable assertions as additional evidence, not as a replacement for the original Lucid record.
Keep thesis nomenclatural status visible for concepts proposed only there.
must_not: Require the user to choose or launch a separate Saitis-group key.
Rewrite Lucid states as though they were Schubert characters.
Present thesis-only proposed names as formally published.

examples.title: Female Saitis-group specimen remains ambiguous

specimen.evidence: Good habitus photographs but no cleared epigyne or associated male

examples.situation: The specimen is consistent with several Saitis-group genera, while the published Schubert key is explicitly male-only and female morphology is conserved or poorly known in some lineages.
expected: Recognise that the published key is not applicable as a female key.
Use source-supported female diagnostic assertions where available.
Preserve multiple genus candidates and state what evidence would be needed to narrow them.
Allow the result to remain unresolved.
must_not: Run male-only key leads against the female as if they were universally applicable.
Manufacture genus certainty from conserved external morphology.
Infer a species from locality alone.

examples.title: Legacy Lucid Maratus sensu lato
examples.situation: The Lucid evidence returns its broad legacy Maratus entity, whose contents span several later concepts.
expected: Preserve LTX043 as the original identification result.
Apply the one-to-many split recorded by CW005 and show the compatible later concepts as a reconciliation layer.
Use additional morphology to distinguish Schubert Maratus sensu stricto from Anablemum, Hypoblemum, Jotus, Micromaratus, Salinatus, Striattus and Variattus where possible.
Keep residual or uncertain legacy contents unresolved.
must_not: Report TC0007 solely because the word Maratus is spelled identically.
Erase the Lucid result after crosswalking it.
Treat every former Lycidas or Lucid Maratus species as a member of Maratus sensu stricto.

examples.title: Prefer an easy observation before a difficult palp character
examples.situation: A dorsal body or leg character and a fine embolic character would reduce the candidate set by nearly the same amount, but the latter needs microscopy and correct palp orientation.
expected: Offer the nearly equally discriminating field-visible character first.
Retain the palp character as a later confirmation option.
Explain the required view or equipment when a microscopic character is requested.
Permit 'not sure' without penalising the candidate taxa.
must_not: Assume that every character has equal observation cost.
Force microscopy when an easier observation provides nearly the same discrimination.
Pretend that observation difficulty is source-measured; it is a future curator/product assessment.

examples.title: Species suggestion follows a genus result

specimen.observed_evidence: Silvery-blue iridescent dorsal opisthosoma with a small central dark patch

examples.situation: Genus-level evidence supports Micromaratus, and the dorsal pattern resembles the source diagnosis for SP0008, Micromaratus bluey.
expected: Show Micromaratus as the primary result.
Show Micromaratus bluey only as a secondary candidate, preferably as diagnostic-if-character-confirmed.
Explain that the relevant pattern must be confirmed under useful lighting and that females are unknown in the thesis treatment.
Keep the thesis-only nomenclatural caveat attached to the proposed species name.
must_not: Replace the genus result with a species label.
Treat the Emerald type locality as independently diagnostic.
Claim certainty from iridescent colour in a poor or angle-dependent photograph.

examples.title: Taxonomy changes after release
examples.situation: A later qualifying publication changes preferred names, availability or concept boundaries after observations have already been stored.
expected: Leave the original Lucid ontology and score evidence unchanged.
Update concept, name-usage and crosswalk records independently.
Re-evaluate presentation of the stored result through the updated mapping while preserving its original provenance.
Retain superseded or conflicting assertions where historical reproducibility requires them.
must_not: Rewrite historical Lucid labels or matrix cells to match the new taxonomy.
Use a taxon name string as the join key.
Destroy the ability to reproduce an identification under the earlier source snapshot.

examples.title: Conflicting source assertions remain visible
examples.situation: Schubert Chapter V names Umbrattus spectabilis as type species in the genus heading, while the composition line labels Umbrattus bimaculatus as type species.
expected: Present both source assertions with their page provenance.
Mark the type-species question unresolved pending author clarification or a qualifying publication.
Continue to use the biological concept and its diagnostic evidence without pretending the nomenclatural conflict is settled.
must_not: Silently choose one type species because it appears first or last.
Overwrite one source assertion with the other.
Convert a draft inconsistency into an accepted nomenclatural act.
